input.question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?
input.ground_truth: Certainly if one considers the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid empire as the "end of antiquity" and the beginning of the early medieval era. It is the last great war because the next one defined the end of the era. Then the question becomes is the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid Empire the best delimiting event between late antiquity and early medieval. There's a lot of good points stating that it is, since the fall of the Sassanid empire meant the Byzantine Empire was then the only surviving great power from classical antiquity. All of the other powers of the era are relatively new. The Muslim conquest of North Africa and Levant also split off those regions from what the classical Roman world. A parallel can be drawn to how the fall of the Soviet Union marked the end of the cold war.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big box of old toys that your grandparents played with. These toys are from "the old times" or "antiquity." Now, there was a big fight (war) between two boys (Heraclius and Khusro II) a long, long time ago. This fight was one of the last really big and important toy battles with those old toys and old ways of playing.

James Howard-Johnston, who is like a grown-up who studies old stories, called this fight "the last great war of antiquity." That means he thinks it was the final super important fight before everything changed and people started using new kinds of toys and new ways to play.

So, he thinks it was justified (that means he had a good reason) to call it that because after this fight, things were never the same as before. The world started to look and act differently, like when you grow up and start playing with new kinds of games instead of your old toys.

But some other grown-ups might say, "Hmm, maybe there were still some important fights after that with new toys." But most people agree with James because this was really the last big fight with the old ways.

So, in simple words: James thought it was the last really big, important fight with the old ways, and that’s why he called it "the last great war of antiquity."
